raw_response:
I farm the way I know best: I keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because it is the steadiest base for my household, and I use the rest for vegetables and stevia to bring in cash during the year. I have well irrigation, so I will not gamble on only rainfed production. I will put better seed and more fertilizer on the crops that repay it clearly, especially wheat, maize, chili, eggplant, cabbage, and cauliflower. For stevia, I will keep inputs moderate because it needs careful management but I do not want to push costs too high. I will plough for wheat and maize to set up the main field well, and I will mostly use rotary tillage for the vegetable and stevia plots because it is faster and suits small plots better. I will irrigate vegetables more often than grain, and I will spray more on chili and eggplant because insects and disease pressure are usually heavier there. This is the balance I would choose between steady grain, cash income, labor I can handle, and the water access I have.
